metric.why: Distributed AI training is unusually intolerant of network degradation; a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage.
metric.metric: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth
metric.definition: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.

reading.body:
Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth are operational metrics for AI data centers, not just networking details, because distributed training wastes GPU-hours before it causes an outage.

The data places this metric in the uptime and redundancy category, alongside UPS battery health, generator runtime, and SLA uptime compliance. That grouping is the point. A facility can hold power continuously and still fail its workload if the internal fabric or external transit degrades. For distributed AI training, the network is part of the uptime surface, not a layer above it.

The stated reason is intolerance: lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage. That makes network measurement a leading indicator rather than a lagging one. Power failures are visible. A rising loss rate is not, until the training run has already burned compute it cannot recover.

What this does not cover is any actual measurement. There are no latency figures, no loss rates, no bandwidth numbers, and no comparison across facilities. It defines the metric and its rationale, and nothing about how any specific data center performs against it.
